Alex — thanks for the demo this morning. Quick recap and asks so we can get you a short formal banded proposal: 

1) Expected monthly token volume (production): please confirm a low/likely/high range (tokens per month).
2) Peak concurrency: what do you expect for 95th and 99th percentile TPS during business hours? Any weekday/weekend differences?
3) Budget target: what is your target $ / 1M tokens (or an annualized budget range we should aim for)?
4) Timeline & procurement: target go-live and any procurement constraints (PO, legal redlines, enterprise SSO/KMS needs).

From our side I'm planning to propose 3 slab bands (conservative / mid / committed) with burst windows and an initial canary allocation in the first 30 days. Attached is a one-pager that summarizes how our hosted pricing bands work and what affects unit economics (batching, caching, model variant).

Attachments: redwood-hosted-pricing-cheatsheet.pdf (PDF)

If you can reply with the numbers above this afternoon, we'll turn that into a formal banded proposal and send a short SOW draft.

Thanks —

Rafael — thanks for the follow-up and for the one-pager. Numbers below based on what we saw in our telemetry + product roadmap assumptions: 

- Expected monthly tokens (prod): Low 8M / Likely 12M / High 18M tokens per month. We expect initial pilot to be ~2-3M for first 30 days then ramp.
- Peak TPS: 95th ~150 TPS, 99th spikes up to ~230 TPS during staggered batch exports (usually 10–12pm PST). Weekend load is about 40% of weekday.
- Budget target: $40–$55 per 1M tokens (we're targeting <$50 if possible; open to committed discount).
- Timeline: Pilot start target Jan 2027; procurement window typical for us is 4–6 weeks (legal requires standard MSA + security appendix). We use DocuSign generally.

Notes: We have a short list of models — most calls are single-turn generation with an average of ~450 tokens per request (so tokens/request matters for the unit math). Also want to understand how burst windows are priced; we'll need a clarification in the proposal on burst caps vs committed TPS.
